title: The Fragmented Mirror
description: Examine the continuity of your identity. Discover if your 'self' feels whole or fragmented during mood collapse.

questions.text: When I am in a deep low, the person I am when I'm 'okay' feels like...

options.text: Me, just having a hard time.
A cousin or a distant friend.
A total stranger / a fake version of me.
I honestly can't remember that person exists.

questions.text: My memories of the last few weeks feel...

options.text: Clear and continuous.
A bit hazy.
Like a movie I watched but wasn't in.
Fragmented; there are gaps in my sense of time.

questions.text: I feel like I am several different 'people' inside me fighting for control...

options.text: No, just normal mood swings.
Sometimes.
Often, and it's exhausting.
Yes, I am a collection of broken pieces.

insight_cloud.title: Dissociative Depression
insight_cloud.text: Depression can create a 'wall' in the mind. When we are low, our brain might disconnect from our 'High' self as a way to save energy. This is called Narrative Fragmentation.

questions.text: When I speak to others, I feel like...

options.text: Authentic and real.
Polite but a bit tired.
Executing a script; I'm not really there.
Watching myself from a corner of the room.

questions.text: Do you feel like your 'center' has gone missing?

options.text: No.
Occasionally.
Frequently.
Yes, there is no one 'home' at the center.
